course_outcomes.co_description: Explain the time and space complexity trade-offs of common linear and non-linear data structures.
Implement arrays, linked lists, stacks, and queues to solve structured programming problems.
Apply tree and graph traversal algorithms to search and organize hierarchical and networked data.
Analyze sorting and searching algorithms using Big-O notation to select the most efficient approach for a given dataset.
Design and implement an original algorithmic solution to a real-world data-processing problem as a capstone project.

topics: Course Orientation & Introduction to Data Structures

llos.outcome_text: Identify the course objectives, key topics, and assessment methods.
Demonstrate correct setup of the Python/C++ development environment.
Value precision in following course requirements and academic policies.
Define time complexity and space complexity using Big-O notation.
Compute the Big-O complexity of simple code snippets.
Value analytical rigor when comparing algorithm efficiency.
Describe the memory layout of static and dynamic arrays.
Implement array insertion, deletion, and resizing operations.
Demonstrate diligence in tracing array operations by hand.
Explain the structure of singly and doubly linked lists.
Implement node insertion, deletion, and traversal for linked lists.
Show commitment to writing clean, well-commented pointer logic.
Explain the LIFO and FIFO principles behind stacks and queues.
Implement a stack and a queue using arrays and linked lists.
Value structured problem decomposition when applying stacks and queues.
Recall and synthesize key concepts covered in Weeks 1-5.
Apply learned skills to solve assessment items accurately.
Demonstrate academic integrity and diligence during examination.
Explain the mechanics of recursive function calls and base cases.
Implement recursive solutions using the divide-and-conquer strategy.
Demonstrate persistence in tracing and debugging recursive calls.
Describe the structure and properties of binary search trees.
Implement insertion, deletion, and lookup operations on a BST.
Value organized, hierarchical thinking when modeling tree data.
Differentiate in-order, pre-order, and post-order traversal strategies.
Implement recursive and iterative tree traversal algorithms.
Demonstrate patience in verifying traversal output against expected results.
Explain the heap property and its use in priority queues.
Implement a min-heap and max-heap with insert and extract operations.
Value efficiency when selecting a data structure for priority-based tasks.
Explain hashing functions and collision resolution strategies.
Implement a hash table using chaining and open addressing.
Demonstrate diligence in testing edge cases such as hash collisions.
Recall and synthesize key concepts covered in Weeks 7-11.
Apply learned skills to solve assessment items accurately.
Demonstrate academic integrity and diligence during examination.
Describe adjacency list and adjacency matrix graph representations.
Implement a graph data structure supporting both representations.
Value clarity when modeling real-world networks as graphs.
Explain the mechanics of breadth-first and depth-first graph traversal.
Implement BFS and DFS to solve connectivity and pathfinding problems.
Demonstrate persistence in debugging traversal edge cases such as cycles.

topics: Sorting Algorithms I: Bubble, Insertion, Selection Sort

llos.outcome_text: Analyze the time complexity of elementary sorting algorithms.
Implement bubble sort, insertion sort, and selection sort.
Value systematic comparison when benchmarking algorithm performance.

topics: Sorting Algorithms II: Merge Sort & Quick Sort

llos.outcome_text: Analyze the divide-and-conquer approach used in merge sort and quick sort.
Implement merge sort and quick sort and compare their performance.
Demonstrate collaboration in pair-programming algorithm benchmarks.
Justify the choice of data structures and algorithms used in the capstone project.
Build and present a working solution to a real-world data-processing problem.
Demonstrate professionalism and ownership when presenting project work.
Recall and synthesize key concepts covered across the entire term.
Apply learned skills to solve comprehensive assessment items accurately.
Demonstrate academic integrity and diligence during examination.
